claims.text: The University of Akron and Case Western Reserve have coauthored more than 200 works since 2012 and hold four joint federal awards.
claims.source: OpenAlex works listing both institutions; NSF awards API
claims.falsified_if: Either measure collapses. This is the claim that refutes the deleted 'nothing suggests they have met' line; if it fails, that line was closer to right than this page is and the page must be withdrawn, not softened. This claim is about collaboration EXISTING, which is what refutes 'never convened'. It is deliberately independent of whether the collaboration is about polymers — see col-rarely-about-polymers, which says it mostly is not.

claims.text: Joint output peaked at 29 papers in 2018, dropped to 11, came back to 22 in 2020, then fell in four straight years to two papers in 2024 and rose to six in 2025; the controlled rate is still 63 percent below the peak. This guards the standfirst's shape sentence, the hero chart's description, the cold open's label and the closer. THE SHAPE MOVED TWICE ON 2026-08-31. The page had been fetched on 2026-08-17 with the window hand-stopped at 2024 and said joint output 'has fallen in each of the last three' years. First, the same keyless OpenAlex call now returns 2025, and 2025 tripled off the 2024 floor. Second, deriving the run instead of counting it showed the run was never three: 2021 already fell from 2020, so the falls into the trough are FOUR, and the sentence before it that put 2021 in a three-year wobble was describing a shape the chart did not draw. The fall is still real and the rebound is one year on six papers, so the page reports both and headlines neither: app.js walks the run back from the lowest year rather than carrying a hand-set three.
claims.source: as above; joint works per 1,000 of Akron's own annual output
claims.assert: D['totals']['peak_year'] == 2018 and D['totals']['peak_joint'] == 29 and max(r['joint'] for r in D['series']) == 29 and D['series'][-1]['year'] == 2025 and (lambda s: s[2019] < s[2018] and s[2020] > s[2019] and s[2021] < s[2020] and s[2022] < s[2021] and s[2023] < s[2022] and s[2024] < s[2023] and s[2024] == 2 and s[2024] == min(s.values()) and s[2025] == 6)({r['year']: r['joint'] for r in D['series']}) and (lambda q: q[2021] < q[2020] and q[2022] < q[2021] and q[2023] < q[2022] and q[2024] < q[2023] and q[2025] > q[2024])({r['year']: r['per_1k_akron'] for r in D['series']}) and round((1 - D['series'][-1]['per_1k_akron'] / max(r['per_1k_akron'] for r in D['series'])) * 100) == 63
claims.actual: [(r['year'], r['joint'], r['akron'], r['per_1k_akron']) for r in D['series']]
claims.falsified_if: The peak moves off 2018 or off 29 works, 2019 stops being the drop or 2020 the rebound, the run of four falls into 2024 breaks or lengthens, 2024 stops being the lowest year at two papers, 2025 stops printing six, the controlled rate stops falling across the same four years or stops rebounding after them, or the end-of-series gap to the peak stops rounding to 63 percent. Any of those and the standfirst, the cold-open label and the closer are describing a shape the chart beneath them does not draw. The 2020 boundary is asserted in both directions because it is what makes the run FOUR rather than three or five, and a hand-set three is the error this claim was rewritten to catch. The falls are asserted on the COUNTS and again on the CONTROLLED RATE, because the closer walks the reader down the rate and the two series could diverge. NOTE the final year is the least-indexed and must not carry this claim alone: the 2018-2024 movement holds without it.

claims.text: The decline is not an artifact of incomplete indexing: Case Western's own output is higher at the end of the series than at the joint peak.
claims.source: OpenAlex, each institution's own works per year
claims.assert: D['series'][-1]['cwru'] >= [r['cwru'] for r in D['series'] if r['year'] == D['totals']['peak_year']][0]
claims.actual: [(r['year'], r['akron'], r['cwru']) for r in D['series'][-4:]]
claims.falsified_if: Case Western's own output drops below its level at the joint peak, which would mean the index is thin on recent years and the joint decline cannot be separated from it. It is the guard that matters most on a refresh: the 2025 year was added on 2026-08-31 and Case Western's own output that year, 6,368, is well above the 5,532 it published in the 2018 peak year, so the series end is not an indexing artifact.

claims.text: Within the window measured here, 2012 to 2025, no new joint federal award started after 2017.
claims.source: NSF awards API, awards to either institution since 2012, Collaborative Research mechanism only
claims.assert: max(int((a['start'] or '0000')[-4:]) for a in D['joint_awards']) <= 2017 and D['meta']['years'][1] == 2025
claims.actual: [(a['start'], a['amount'], a['title'][:60]) for a in D['joint_awards']] + [('window', D['meta']['years'])]
claims.falsified_if: A joint award starting after 2017 and inside the window appears, OR the pull is extended past 2025 without re-reading this sentence. The window end is asserted as an EQUALITY for exactly that reason, and it did its job on 2026-08-31: the pull moved from 2024 to 2025 and this claim failed until every sentence carrying a window year had been re-read. LIMIT, and it has already bitten: the unbounded form of this claim ('none since 2017') was refutable from PIC's own timeline page, which records the CWRU-led NEO-SMART NSF Engine awarded 2026-07-14. That award is outside this window, so the arithmetic held while the sentence did not. Separately, this sees NSF only: a joint NIH, DOE, EDA or state award would not appear here and would not falsify the arithmetic while still making the sentence misleading.

claims.text: These instruments can demonstrate collaboration and cannot demonstrate its absence.
claims.source: Method note, not a data check
claims.falsified_if: Nothing in the data can falsify this; it is the standing limit on how the page may be read, and it is the reason a null result would not have been published.

claims.text: Of 208 joint papers, eight are classified in polymers and plastics and eleven in biomaterials, nineteen in all, about nine percent. The four years 2021 to 2024 carry no joint paper in either subject; 2025 carries one, the first since 2020.
claims.source: OpenAlex subfields 2507 and 2502, confirmed against the s3://openalex snapshot; a classification, not a keyword
claims.assert: D['totals']['subject_total'] < 0.15 * D['totals']['coauthored'] and D['totals']['polymer_total'] == 8 and D['totals']['bio_total'] == 11 and D['totals']['last_subject_year'] == 2025 and all(r['polymer'] + r['bio'] == 0 for r in D['series'] if 2021 <= r['year'] <= 2024) and one(r['polymer'] for r in D['series'] if r['year'] == 2025) == 1 and sorted(r['year'] for r in D['series'] if r['polymer'] + r['bio'])[-2] == 2020
claims.actual: [(r['year'], r['polymer'], r['bio']) for r in D['series']] + [(D['totals']['coauthored'], D['totals']['subject_total'], D['totals']['last_subject_year'])]
claims.falsified_if: The subject share rises above 15 percent, either subject count moves off eight and eleven, or the four-year silence from 2021 to 2024 gains a paper. THE SENTENCE THIS GUARDS WAS INVERTED BY A REFRESH: it read 'the last of either was 2020', which was a four-year silence written as a date, and the 2026-08-31 pull put one polymer paper in 2025 and made it read as recency. It now measures the silence, which is what it was always about. THIS NUMBER ALSO MOVED WHEN THE BOUND DID: the full-text keyword 'polymer' returned 24 of these papers and the subject classification returns eight, because the keyword counted any paper that mentioned the word. The larger number was the one published first.
